title: Federal Rotational Cyber Workforce Program Act of 2021
official_summary:
Federal Rotational Cyber Workforce Program Act of 2021

This bill establishes a rotational cyber workforce program under which certain federal employees may be detailed among rotational cyber workforce positions at other agencies.

This bill authorizes an agency to determine whether a workforce position involving information technology, cybersecurity, or other cyber-related functions in that agency is eligible for the program.

Additionally, the bill requires the Office of Personnel Management to issue a Federal Rotational Cyber Workforce Program operation plan providing policies, processes, and procedures for detailing employees among rotational cyber workforce positions at agencies.

The Government Accountability Office must assess the operation and effectiveness of the rotational cyber workforce program by addressing the extent to which agencies have participated in the program and the experiences of employees serving in the program.

summary.headline: This law creates a program that lets federal cybersecurity and IT workers temporarily move between jobs at different federal agencies.
summary.what_it_does: The law sets up a rotational cyber workforce program, which allows certain federal employees to be detailed, or temporarily assigned, to cyber-related jobs at other federal agencies. Each agency can decide whether its own information technology, cybersecurity, or other cyber positions qualify for the program. The Office of Personnel Management must issue an operation plan with the rules, steps, and procedures for these assignments. The Government Accountability Office must later review how well the program works, including how many agencies take part and what employees experience.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees in information technology and cybersecurity roles
who_it_affects.how: Certain of them may be temporarily detailed to cyber-related positions at other federal agencies under the program.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies with cyber, IT, or information technology positions
who_it_affects.how: Each agency decides which of its positions are eligible for the rotational program and takes part in detailing employees under the plan.
The office must write and issue an operation plan that sets policies, processes, and procedures for the program.
The office must assess the program's operation and effectiveness, including agency participation and employee experiences.
